r0056.title: Винительный (Akkusativ) или Дательный (Dativ) падеж для возвратного местоимения (Reflexivpronomen)
r0056.titleEn: Akkusativ or Dativ for the Reflexivpronomen
r0056.content_md_en:
### How to check whether the Reflexivpronomen takes the Akkusativ or the Dativ

1. Find the verb.
2. Find what the action is aimed at.
3. Cross out everything that stands after a preposition (für, über, auf, zum, mit, in – any of them).
4. Is anything left that the verb's action is aimed at directly?
   Yes → the reflexive pronoun goes in the Dativ.
   No → the reflexive pronoun goes in the Akkusativ.

### Why do we cross out the noun after a preposition?
A noun after a preposition belongs to that preposition, not to what the verb's action is aimed at directly. That is why it has no bearing on the case of the reflexive pronoun.
zum Geburtstag → when?
mit den Verkäufern → with whom?
in kleine Läden → where to?
für ein Gericht → what for?

### How to handle a subordinate clause (Nebensatz)
If the subordinate clause fills the slot of what the action is aimed at, it counts when you choose the case.
was / wer / ob / dass → the clause itself is what the action is aimed at → the reflexive pronoun goes in the Dativ
weil / wenn / obwohl → this is an adverbial → cross it out

Exceptions: wo, wie – these depend on the context.

### How to work through the exceptions: wo and wie
wo and wie can operate in two modes – the question you put to the subordinate clause decides which one.

OBJECT mode (question “What?”) → Dativ
If the clause answers the question “What?”, it works like dass – that is, it stands in for the direct object.
Ich schaue mir an, wie du kochst. – I watch [what?] how you cook.
Ich merke mir, wo du wohnst. – I note [what?] where you live.
Logic: it is an object → the reflexive pronoun is strictly in the Dativ (mir).

ADVERBIAL mode (questions “Where?”, “How?”) → Akkusativ
If the clause is mere decoration – an adverbial of place or manner rather than an object of the verb – it is crossed out under the general rule (see above).
Ich wasche mich, wo es Wasser gibt. – I wash [where?] where there is water.
Ich verhalte mich, wie du gesagt hast. – I behave [how?] the way you said.
Logic: there is no noun serving as the direct object, the clause answers “where/how” → cross it out → the reflexive pronoun goes in the Akkusativ (mich).
r0056.examplesEn:
Ich kaufe mir ein Auto. – mir is in the Dativ, because the Akkusativ slot is already taken by “ein Auto” (something is left that the action is aimed at).
Ich wasche mich. – mich is in the Akkusativ, there is no other object of the action, the verb is purely reflexive.
Ich wünsche mir, dass du kommst. – the dass-clause stands in the object slot → mir in the Dativ.
Ich freue mich, weil du kommst. – the weil-clause is crossed out as an adverbial → a plain Akkusativ is left (mich).
r0056.noteEn: Some verbs do not take part in this decision at all – they demand the Dativ outright, with no alternatives and no direct object of the action (helfen, gefallen, danken and the like). The rule simply does not apply to them.

r0027.title: Verben mit Dativ und Akkusativ
r0027.content_md_en:
### Verben mit Dativ und Akkusativ – verbs with two objects

Some verbs are followed by TWO objects at once: to whom (Dativ) + what (Akkusativ).

**Role** | **Case** | **Question** | **Articles (m / f / n / Pl)**
Person 1 | Nominativ | Wer? | der · die · das · die / ein · eine · ein · –
Person 2 | Dativ | Wem? | dem · der · dem · den / einem · einer · einem · –
Objekt | Akkusativ | Was? | den · die · das · die / einen · eine · ein · –

💡 Order: Subject → Verb → **Dativ** → **Akkusativ** (to whom → what)
💡 The indefinite article has no plural form (the noun simply goes without one)
r0027.examplesEn:
**Example** | **Translation**||
Ich gebe dem Mann das Buch. | I give the man the book.||
Er schenkt der Frau einen Ring. | He gives the woman a ring.||
Wir zeigen den Kindern die Stadt. | We show the children the city.||
r0027.noteEn: Typical verbs: geben, schenken, zeigen, bringen, schicken, kaufen, erklären, empfehlen, leihen, schreiben, wünschen, anbieten. Check: ask two questions – “to whom?” (Wem? → Dativ) and “what?” (Was? → Akkusativ). Order with two nouns: Dativ before Akkusativ.

r0055.title: s = es – разговорное стяжение
r0055.content_md_en:
### 's = es (colloquial contraction)
In casual speech the pronoun es often merges with the preceding word through an apostrophe:
Wie geht's? = Wie geht es? (How are you?)
Wenn's regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause. = Wenn es regnet... (If it rains...)
Gibt's noch Kaffee? = Gibt es noch Kaffee?
💡 It works after verbs (geht's, gibt's) and after conjunctions (wenn's, dass') – 's is always = es
r0055.examplesEn:
Wie geht's? – How are you?
Wenn's regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause. – If it rains, I'll stay at home.
Gibt's noch Kaffee? – Is there any coffee left?

r0058.title: Infinitiv mit zu
r0058.content_md_en:
### Infinitiv mit zu

The pattern "..., zu + Infinitiv" is a compressed replacement for a dass-clause, used when the subject is the same in both parts. The second subject is not repeated, and the main verb moves to the end with zu in front of it.

Ich finde es wichtig, dass ich den Garten sauber halte. → Ich finde es wichtig, den Garten sauber zu halten.

Typical verbs and expressions that take a zu-Infinitiv:
es ist wichtig / es ist möglich / es ist nötig (impersonal constructions)
vergessen (to forget), versuchen (to try), hoffen (to hope), anfangen (to begin), aufhören (to stop), vorhaben (to plan), sich freuen (to be glad) and so on

### With separable verbs zu goes BETWEEN the prefix and the stem
Not "zu abschließen", but abzuschließen – prefix + zu + stem, written as one word.
ab + zu + schließen → abzuschließen
an + zu + rufen → anzurufen

### The difference from constructions WITHOUT zu
zu is not used:
after modal verbs (können, müssen, wollen...): Ich kann kommen. (not zu kommen)
in the Futur with werden: Ich werde kommen.
after lassen/sehen/hören + Infinitiv: Ich lasse ihn kommen. / Ich sehe ihn kommen.
r0058.examplesEn:
Ich finde es wichtig, den Garten sauber zu halten. – I think it is important to keep the garden clean.
Vergessen Sie nicht, die Haustür abzuschließen. – Do not forget to lock the front door.
Sie hat vor, nächstes Jahr umzuziehen. – She is planning to move next year.
Er hört auf, Süßigkeiten zu essen. – He is giving up sweets.
r0058.noteEn:
Check: if the phrase can be unpacked into a full dass-clause and the subject there would be THE SAME as in the main clause – compress it into a zu-Infinitiv and do not repeat the second subject. If the subjects differ, a zu-Infinitiv is impossible and you need a full dass-Satz (or damit, if it expresses a purpose).

zu + Infinitiv is a sentence compressed from a dass-clause, used when the subject (Subjekt) is one and the same. With different subjects zu + Infinitiv is impossible, you need a full clause with dass or damit.

r0059.title: sondern – "не X, а Y"
r0059.content_md_en:
### sondern – "not X, but Y"

sondern is used only after a negation (kein/nicht), when one statement is rejected and the correct one is given instead.

Ich kaufe kein Brot, sondern Kuchen. – I am not buying bread, but cake.

### What can be negated with sondern
Any part of the sentence can be negated and replaced, not just a noun:
Noun: kein Brot, sondern Kuchen
Adjective: nicht schön, sondern hässlich
Adverb: nicht heute, sondern morgen
Verb/action: Er singt nicht, sondern tanzt. – He is not singing, he is dancing.

### Word order
sondern is a coordinating conjunction (like aber/und/oder), position 0, and the word order after it does not change.

⚠ Do not confuse it with aber: aber is a plain "but" (a contrast with no negation in the first part), while sondern must follow nicht/kein and replaces what was rejected with what is correct.
r0059.examplesEn:
Ich kaufe kein Brot, sondern Kuchen. – I am not buying bread, but cake.
Das ist nicht mein Buch, sondern deins. – That is not my book, but yours.
Er singt nicht, sondern tanzt. – He is not singing, he is dancing.
Sie kommt nicht heute, sondern morgen. – She is coming not today, but tomorrow.
r0059.noteEn: sondern – only after a negation (kein/nicht); it replaces what is negated with the correct version. It can negate and replace any part of speech – noun, adjective, adverb, verb – not only nouns.
